notes: PSA 7.4 ng/mL. PI-RADS 3. PSAD 0.16. Prostate volume 45 mL. csPCa 0.62.

note_sections.t: Re-evaluation of rising PSA and prior negative biopsy to determine the most appropriate management strategy.

Recently retired self-employed contractor (carpentry) with a history of hypercholesterolaemia managed with simvastatin and rosuvastatin. The patient has experienced a steady rise in PSA levels over the past three years, from 3.3 ng/mL in May 2022 to 7.4 ng/mL in February 2025. A previous systematic biopsy was performed and returned negative for malignancy. He reports moderate lower urinary tract symptoms, with an IPSS score of 19/35, but no haematuria or bone pain. Socially, he is married, lives alone, and consumes approximately three units of alcohol per week. He is currently undergoing routine foot care with a podiatrist. The patient is hard of hearing and prefers written summaries for clarity.

On DRE, the prostate is symmetrically enlarged and non-nodular, consistent with a clinical stage of cT1c. General examination is unremarkable, with normal cardiopulmonary findings and no palpable lymphadenopathy or spinal tenderness.
